title: Three-norm bound for multilinear polynomials
statement: Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$, let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $F$ be a real coefficient family on the subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ whose coefficients vanish on sets of cardinality greater than $k$. Suppose $X_1,\ldots,X_n$ are independent real random variables, each with mean $0$ and second moment $1$, and that each $X_i$ is $(2,3,\rho)$-hypercontractive for some $0<\rho<1$. Then the square of the real-valued $L^3$ norm of the random-input multilinear evaluation of $F$ is at most $(1/\rho)^{2k}\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}F(S)^2$.
hypotheses_covered: $F$ is a coefficient family on subsets of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$
